title: Paragraph Heading Changed to Cell-5 Heading

illustrates.quote: Changing Paragraph Headings to Cell-5 or Cell-7 Headings. A paragraph heading may provide better navigation for the braille reader when it is separated from the paragraph and changed to a cell-5 or cell-7 heading. (See Sample 4-5: Paragraph Headings Relocated on page 4-20 and Sample 4-6: Paragraph Heading Changed to Cell-5 Heading on page 4-21.)

blocks.features: Bold blue run-in heading in print, opening the first paragraph; relocated to its own cell-5 line in braille because its effect covers the whole passage (this paragraph AND the bulleted item that follows), per rule 4.8.3.b.

blocks.text: With kettles and steamers, chefs can prepare large amounts of food efficiently.
blocks.features: Plain body text, follows the elevated heading.

blocks.text: **Steam-Jacketed Kettle.** Available in both freestanding and tabletop models, a **steam-jacketed kettle** is a kettle that provides an even heat by circulating steam through its walls.
blocks.features: Bulleted list item whose own bold run-in lead phrase, 'Steam-Jacketed Kettle.', covers only this one paragraph and is therefore left INLINE (not elevated), wrapped only in an emphasis/typeform indicator pair, per rule 4.8.2/4.8.3.b's scope test.

print.notes: Two print run-in headings of different scope: 'Kettles and Steamers' covers the whole passage and is elevated to its own cell-5 line in braille, per 4.8.3.b, while 'Steam-Jacketed Kettle.' covers only its own single bulleted paragraph and is left inline as an ordinary (emphasized) paragraph heading -- the section's clearest illustration of the scope test that decides between rule 4.8.2's two outcomes.
print.printFeatures: Bold blue section-level run-in heading followed by a plain paragraph, then a bulleted sub-item with its own smaller bold run-in heading.

lines: provides an ev5 h1t by circulat+ /1m
braille.notes: Line 1 the cell-5 heading 'Kettles and Steamers', elevated per 4.8.3.b; lines 2-3 its paragraph, ending '444'; line 4 blank; lines 5-9 the bulleted sub-item, whose own run-in heading 'Steam-Jacketed Kettle.' stays inline, wrapped in a typeform (bold) indicator pair (also re-applied where print repeats the term in bold mid-paragraph).

uncertain: Both paragraphs in this file are longer in print than what the braille excerpt actually transcribes -- each is cut off with a '444' continuation/ellipsis marker (line 3 and, originally, the end of the bulleted item) with no print.blocks equivalent for 'more text omitted here', matching the same convention documented for sample-4-01. print.blocks is trimmed to match exactly what the braille excerpt itself gives, per the 'transcribe only what the source shows' convention, rather than the fuller print sentence.

The first paragraph directly follows its heading with no blank line -- its flush first line versus Emboss's ordinary 2-cell indent is the same standards-findings.md F-39 gap seen throughout this section.
resolution: Runs agree on every field (kind/level/text and braille.lines); only prose wording differed (merged). During model-building verification, both paragraphs needed trimming to match exactly what the braille excerpt transcribes (each is cut short with a '444' continuation marker, matching sample-4-01's own documented convention), and the bulleted item's mid-sentence repeat of “steam-jacketed kettle” needed its own **bold** markup (braille repeats the typeform indicator there, per the file's own braille.notes).
